title: Nakanishi2015 – SSVEP Nakanishi 2015 dataset
description: A 12-class steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) EEG dataset using joint frequency-phase modulation, recorded from 9 healthy participants (the original study reports 10) in a simulated online brain-computer interface experiment. Eight occipital and parieto-occipital channels were recorded at 256 Hz while participants gazed at flickering targets on a 4x3 virtual keypad. The data were originally used to compare canonical correlation analysis (CCA) based methods for SSVEP detection.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a Biosemi ActiveTwo amplifier from 8 channels (PO7, PO3, POz, PO4, PO8, O1, Oz, O2) with CMS/DRL reference. Each of 15 blocks contained 12 trials, one per stimulus frequency from 9.25 to 14.75 Hz. A red square cued the target for 1 s, then all stimuli flickered for 4 s on a 60 Hz LCD monitor. Data were downsampled to 256 Hz and bandpass filtered at 6-80 Hz with zero-phase IIR filtering, and epochs were extracted with a 135 ms delay to allow for visual latency.
